excerpt: Compare family rentals in Al Majaz and Al Taawun by the actual apartment, school and work routes, lease terms and complete annual cost.
introduction:
Al Majaz and Al Taawun both have Sharjah apartment buildings that may suit families, but the best rental depends on the exact tower, household routine and lease. Inspect the home, test the school and work journeys and compare the full cost rather than choosing solely by the area name.

The figures below show how a household can compare rental costs over the same period. The calculation uses a consistent set of inputs to compare the two rental choices.
takeaways: Compare the apartment layout, building condition and actual route to the family's destinations.
Include utilities, transport, non-refundable charges and move-in deposits alongside annual rent.
Review the written lease and confirm the current Sharjah attestation process.

sections.heading: How do the areas differ?
sections.body:
[Bayut's Al Majaz guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-majaz/) describes apartment buildings around the Khaled Lagoon and Buhaira Corniche. Its [Al Taawun guide](https://www.bayut.com/area-guides/al-taawun/) describes a district near the Sharjah–Dubai border with apartment towers and local services. Both descriptions are broad; check the precise building, parking and street.

Visit the building at school and work departure times as well as in the evening. Walk from the entrance to the services the family will use and check crossings, lift access and space for a pushchair if relevant. Inspect the outlook from the specific apartment and its outdoor areas.

The [Sharjah family living guide](/journal/sharjah-real-estate-family-living) provides wider context for the household's location search.

sections.heading: Compare the family's annual cost
sections.body:
Imagine an Al Majaz rental with AED 55,000 annual rent and AED 14,000 of combined utilities and transport. A sample Al Taawun option has AED 52,000 rent and AED 20,000 of those costs. Their totals are AED 69,000 and AED 72,000 respectively. Use the example to compare the rental costs and practical features that matter to your household.

The chart covers only rent, utilities and transport. Add school transport, parking, insurance, non-refundable fees and other differences for your household. Treat refundable deposits as cash needed at move-in and record any eventual deduction separately.

A lower annual amount may not be the best choice if the layout or travel time does not work. Compare homes of similar size and condition and use written terms.

sections.heading: Inspect the apartment and building
sections.body:
Check the bedroom layout, storage, kitchen, cooling, water pressure, windows and visible moisture. Confirm the allocated parking and access from it to the apartment. Ask whether cooling or any utilities are included, how they are billed and who handles repairs.

Inspect lifts, corridors, entry controls and the condition of shared facilities. If a pool or play area matters, confirm it serves the building and is currently operating. Ask about noise and visit at a second time if possible.

Agree a dated condition record and furniture inventory where relevant. Record existing marks and repairs before moving in, and retain a copy with the lease and receipts.

sections.heading: Check school and work journeys
sections.body:
Ask the school about places, fees and bus service for the exact address. Test the journey from the home at the time of the actual school run, including the return. If an adult commutes to Dubai, test the entire route rather than assuming an area near the border is fastest for every workplace.

Include fuel, parking, tolls or public transport and any second vehicle in the budget. Check alternatives for days when the usual route or car is unavailable. The time and cost for other household members to reach shops and healthcare also matter.

A map or advertised travel time is a starting point. Actual access depends on the building entrance, route and time of day.

sections.heading: Read and attest the lease
sections.body:
Request the full rent schedule, security deposit, brokerage and other charges, maintenance responsibilities, renewal, notice and early-exit terms. Verify the landlord or representative's authority and the payment recipient. Ask how the deposit will be assessed and returned.

Sharjah Municipality's [residential tenancy contract template](https://portal.shjmun.gov.ae/en/eservices/Attachements/Residential-Tenancy-Contract-Template.pdf) describes attestation and the parties' obligations under the referenced law. Confirm the current procedure, deadline and charges with the municipality for your agreement; do not rely on an old fee quoted elsewhere.

Keep the attested contract, receipts, meter readings and inventory. Obtain qualified advice if a clause or the responsibilities are unclear.

sections.heading: Plan the move-in cash
sections.body:
Put the first rent payment, deposit, non-refundable fees, utility connection, moving and furniture on a calendar. Ask whether the building requires a move-in permit or refundable deposit and confirm its return conditions. A deposit may be returned later but still reduces the cash available at the start.

Record the remaining rent instalments and school payments as well. If two large payments fall in the same month, plan for them before signing. Keep a reserve for unexpected household costs.

Ask which utility accounts must be opened and whether the previous balance has been settled. Confirm the connection date and any deposit with the provider. If the home is furnished, agree the inventory and condition of appliances so that the move-in record matches what the family actually receives.

sections.heading: Ask about current rentals
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) for local context and ask which relevant Al Majaz or Al Taawun rentals are currently available. Ask for the lease terms and the current availability of the apartment you want to view.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, bedrooms and school or work destinations. Request the exact address and written terms, then view the actual apartment.
